A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DPA/HALVA work and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Renumbered and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V2 reports original HALVA benchmark evaluations, training ablations, and qualitative comparisons in Section 4 and Appendices C and E.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds general-task results, linguistic-quality evaluation, and statistical analyses.

M1.justification: Generative phrase replacement, phrase-level alignment, forward-KL regularization, and LoRA training remain unchanged. Equations (1)–(3), Appendix A pseudocode, and the training hyperparameters match across versions.

E1.justification: V3 adds LLaVA-Bench-in-the-Wild to general vision-language evaluation. Visual Genome training coverage and the previously evaluated benchmarks, including appendix POPE evaluations, remain.

E2.justification: V3 adds MEMVR and AGLA to CHAIR, MEMVR/ARA/AGLA to MME-Hall, and CODE to MMHal-Bench (Tables 1, 2, and 4). VILA-based general-task comparisons expand. Several reference models lose AMBER subtask comparisons, although their aggregate comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Appendix C.10 introduces evaluation of 100 randomly selected AMBER descriptions using GPT-4o-mini and four linguistic criteria scored from 0 to 10. V3 also evaluates VILA/HALVA13B/384 on additional general benchmarks. Existing training budgets and settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Figure S5 examines training stability across existing augmentation subsets, and Appendix C.10 tests whether DPA damages linguistic quality. Earlier loss, reference-model, reference-data, and augmentation ablations, including the HA-DPO transfer experiment, remain.

E5.justification: V2 reports three evaluations and standard deviations for GPT-based evaluations. V3 retains that practice and adds broad significance testing in Appendix C.11 and Tables S11–S14, reporting sample counts, standard errors, and a stated 95% decision rule. No increase in repeated evaluations is stated.

E6.justification: V3 substantially expands reported outcomes with LLaVA-Bench-in-the-Wild, additional VILA general-task scores, new comparators, linguistic-quality ratings, and significance findings. Most retained HALVA scores stay fixed. LLaVA-7B AMBER subtask F1s change from 64.6/65.6/62.4 to 83.3/64.6/65.6 (v2 Table 3; v3 Table S5), while some reference-model subtask results disappear. Table 5 corrects the HALVA13B improvement annotation from 2.16 to 2.60.

T1.justification: Appendix C.11 newly formalizes the score difference, binomial-style standard error, and Adjusted Delta = Delta − 1.96 × SE decision rule. The DPA mathematical definitions, loss formulations, and Appendix B comparison with DPO remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that phrase-level alignment mitigates hallucination while preserving general capabilities, with the same headline improvements of 13.4% F1 and 4.2% hallucination-rate reduction. V3's abstract emphasizes the sequence-level tradeoff already discussed in v2.

C2.justification: V3 adds the explanation that forward KL avoids reverse-KL mode-seeking and contrasts localized hallucination feedback with helpfulness alignment. It interprets new analyses as supporting training stability and preserved linguistic quality. The limitations paragraph is unchanged and merely moved to Appendix F.

D1.justification: V3 replaces the repository-link placeholder with a concrete access address, discloses 28K unique phrase pairs and 5K unique hallucinated objects, and supplies the linguistic-evaluation prompt and benchmark sample counts. These additions document access and evaluation details without changing the retained training recipe.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds substantial positioning against offline preference optimization and token-level/process-reward alignment, with new references including Azar, Amini, Mudgal, and Zeng. It also distinguishes DPA from Gunjal et al.'s subsequence-feedback approach and incorporates newer hallucination baselines.

P1.justification: V3 changes the title, affiliations, and publication header, selectively rewrites the introduction, expands related work, and moves limitations into Appendix F. Most methodological and experimental prose and the principal section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Beyond conference-template changes, Figure 3 is rearranged, Table 3 is condensed with selected details moved into Table S5, and Table 6 gains columns, rows, and significance markings. New training-curve and evaluation-prompt figures and five analysis tables substantially expand the displays; existing qualitative examples remain.

improvement.justification: V3 better examines preservation of general capabilities through added benchmark coverage, fuller VILA evaluation, and direct linguistic-quality assessment, while improving research positioning and code-access information. The gain is limited: AMBER prose reports 80.0 where Table S5 gives 77.1, and Appendix C.11's single-model binomial standard error does not adequately justify all comparisons involving F1 or graded scores. Most established evidence remains unchanged.
